description: I am a Computer Science student passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems through creative thinking. With experience in entrepreneurship, product development, debating, and building technology-driven projects, I enjoy exploring ideas beyond conventional boundaries. I aspire to contribute to impactful innovations at the intersection of technology, science, and space exploration.
summary: Our project is an interactive space exploration experience built around three connected sections, each accessible directly from the website's header. The Film is a 90-second animated treasure hunt that introduces visitors to the story of space exploration through a rocket launch, the Apollo mission to the Moon, objects left behind by astronauts, and NASA's Opportunity rover on Mars. It concludes by showing how a laser sent from Earth can still bounce off a mirror placed on the Moon decades ago. Using real NASA models, photographs and AI-generated narration, the film makes these discoveries engaging and easy to understand. The Signal Console is the main interactive experience, where visitors use a rotary tuning knob to explore 30 space objects across four chapters. Each object has its own record containing its location, mass, date and photograph, supported by a signal log, an interactive Moon and Mars map, and laser-ranging information. The Hardware Bay is a 3D workspace where visitors can explore rovers, landers and satellites through a timeline, rotate models, take them apart and learn about individual components. It also includes guided tours, a true-size mode and a find-the-part game. Together, these three experiences create a journey from storytelling to discovery and hands-on learning, making space exploration more engaging and accessible. The complete project is available in our team's GitHub repository.
details:
Our project is an interactive space exploration platform designed to make NASA's historic missions and discoveries more engaging, accessible and educational. It consists of three connected experiences: an animated film, an interactive Signal Console and a 3D Hardware Bay. The film introduces visitors to important space discoveries through a 90-second animated treasure hunt. The Signal Console allows users to explore 30 space objects across four chapters, with detailed records, photographs, maps and signal information. The Hardware Bay takes learning further by allowing visitors to interact with 3D models of rovers, landers and satellites, explore their internal components and understand how they work.

The main benefit of our project is that it turns traditional space-related information into an interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading facts, users can discover, listen, navigate and examine objects themselves. Our intended impact is to make space science more approachable, especially for younger audiences, while encouraging curiosity about astronomy, engineering and scientific research.

We used modern web development technologies, interactive 3D modelling, animation, NASA's publicly available scientific resources and AI-powered narration to build the experience. Creativity played a major role in connecting storytelling, real scientific evidence and hands-on exploration into one platform. During development, we considered user experience, accessibility, scientific accuracy, visual consistency, performance and ease of navigation to ensure that the project remained educational without becoming difficult to use.
